slides.headline: Pre-season legs feeling like lead?
slides.sub: Where remedial massage fits when your training load ramps up.

slides.title: Training load does the most
slides.body: Pre-season usually means more running, sprints and gym in a short space of time. Heavy legs are common. Sleep, food and sensible load planning do most of the recovery work.

slides.title: Where massage can help
slides.body: Massage can help muscles feel looser and ease that heavy, tight feeling for a while. Many players find it helps them move more comfortably into the next session.

slides.title: Time it around hard sessions
slides.body: Firmer work often suits a day or two before a big session, not the night before. After a heavy block of training, lighter pressure usually feels better than deep work.

slides.title: Tell your therapist your week
slides.body: Let your remedial massage therapist know what training looks like this week and when your next trial or practice match is. They can adjust pressure and focus areas to suit.

slides.title: Massage doesn't replace rehab
slides.body: If a niggle keeps coming back or gets worse with training, massage may ease it for a bit, but it needs an assessment. Our team can refer you to a physio when needed.

slides.headline: Big pre-season block ahead?
slides.body: Our remedial massage therapists tailor each session to your training week and work alongside our physios when needed. Book online via the link in bio.

caption:
Pre-season has started and your legs feel like they belong to someone twice your age?

More kilometres, more sprints and more gym sessions all land at once, so heavy, tight legs are pretty normal. Sleep, food and a sensible ramp-up in training do most of the recovery work.

Remedial massage can be a helpful extra. It often eases that tight, heavy feeling for a while, and the timing matters: firmer work a day or two before a hard session, lighter work after a big block. If a niggle keeps coming back, that's a job for an assessment, not just more massage.

Our remedial massage therapists at Hybrid Physiotherapy work closely with our physios. Book online via the link in bio.

General information only — not a substitute for an individual assessment.
